findings.text: Prototype pollution. A key such as `__proto__[polluted]` is parsed to the path `['__proto__','polluted']`. `target['__proto__']` is `Object.prototype`, which is truthy and an object, so it is not replaced with a fresh array. The recursion then assigns `Object.prototype.polluted = value` (line 43-45). `constructor[prototype][x]` pollutes the same way. Attacker-controlled FormData field names can therefore modify every object's prototype.

A third entry with the same key nests the earlier values instead of appending. After `a=1, a=2, a=3`, `target.a` is `[[1,2],3]` rather than `[1,2,3]`, because `[target[name], value]` wraps the existing array each time.

0.reason: parsePropPath turns `__proto__[polluted]` into ['__proto__','polluted']. On a plain object, `target['__proto__']` is Object.prototype, which is truthy and passes isObject, so it is not replaced. The recursive call then assigns the value onto Object.prototype, and nothing filters out `__proto__` or `constructor`.

1.reason: Line 43 always does `target[name] = [target[name], value]`, even when target[name] is already an array. A third value with the same key therefore produces [[1,2],3] instead of [1,2,3].
